subject: Digital Logic

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems, Binary Arithmetic and Codes
questions.text: Convert the decimal number $(431.625)_{10}$ into: (a) Binary, (b) Octal, and (c) Hexadecimal. Perform the subtraction $(28)_{10} - (45)_{10}$ using 8-bit 2's complement binary arithmetic and indicate overflow.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra, Logic Gates and K-Map Minimization
questions.text: State and prove De Morgan's Theorems algebraically and using truth tables. Simplify the Boolean function $F(A, B, C, D) = (A + B + C)(A + B' + C)(A + B + C')(A + B' + C')$ to minimum product-of-sums (POS) form.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra, Logic Gates and K-Map Minimization
questions.text: Minimize the Boolean function using a 4-variable K-map: $F(A, B, C, D) = \sum m(0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15) + d(1, 6)$. Implement the minimal SOP expression using only 2-input NAND gates.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra, Logic Gates and K-Map Minimization
questions.text: Simplify the Boolean function using Quine-McCluskey (Tabulation Method): $F(A, B, C, D) = \sum m(1, 3, 4, 5, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15)$. Find all prime implicants and essential prime implicants.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra, Logic Gates and K-Map Minimization
questions.text: Design a Full Adder circuit using: (a) Basic logic gates, and (b) Two Half Adders and an OR gate. Explain 4-bit Carry Look-Ahead Adder and show how it reduces carry propagation delay from $O(n)$ to $O(1)$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra, Logic Gates and K-Map Minimization
questions.text: Design a 4-to-16 line decoder using five 2-to-4 line decoders with active-low enable inputs. Implement the Boolean function $F(A, B, C, D) = \sum m(1, 3, 7, 9, 11, 15)$ using a single 8-to-1 Multiplexer.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Sequential Logic Circuits, Flip-Flops and State Tables
questions.text: Explain the Race-Around Condition in JK Flip-Flop. How is race-around avoided using a Master-Slave JK Flip-Flop? Draw its logic diagram and timing waveforms. Convert a JK flip-flop into a D flip-flop and T flip-flop.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Sequential Logic Circuits, Flip-Flops and State Tables
questions.text: Derive characteristic equations and excitation tables for SR, JK, D, and T flip-flops. Construct excitation maps for all four flip-flops.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Sequential Logic Circuits, Flip-Flops and State Tables
questions.text: Design a Synchronous 3-bit Up/Down Gray Code Counter using T flip-flops with a control signal $M$ ($M=0$ for up counting, $M=1$ for down counting). Draw the state diagram, excitation table, K-maps, and logic circuit.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Sequential Logic Circuits, Flip-Flops and State Tables
questions.text: Explain 4-bit Universal Shift Register with mode control inputs $S_1S_0$ (00: Hold, 01: Shift-right, 10: Shift-left, 11: Parallel load). Draw the schematic diagram using 4-to-1 multiplexers and D flip-flops.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Sequential Logic Circuits, Flip-Flops and State Tables
questions.text: Compare Mealy Machine vs. Moore Machine with block diagrams and timing diagrams. Design a Mealy finite state machine to detect the overlapping bit sequence `1011` in a serial input data stream using D flip-flops.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Memory Units and Programmable Logic Devices
questions.text: Compare Programmable Logic Devices: Read-Only Memory (ROM), Programmable Array Logic (PAL), and Programmable Logic Array (PLA). Implement the functions $F_1(A, B, C) = \sum m(0, 1, 3, 5, 7)$ and $F_2(A, B, C) = \sum m(1, 2, 4, 7)$ using a suitable PLA program table and logic diagram.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems, Binary Arithmetic and Codes
questions.text: Explain BCD (8421), Excess-3, and Gray codes. Why is Gray code called a reflected/unit-distance code? Design a combinational logic circuit to convert a 4-bit Binary code into its equivalent 4-bit Gray code using XOR gates.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra, Logic Gates and K-Map Minimization
questions.text: Minimize the following 5-variable Boolean function using 5-variable K-map: $F(A, B, C, D, E) = \sum m(0, 1, 4, 5, 16, 17, 21, 25, 29) + d(9, 11, 13, 15)$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems, Binary Arithmetic and Codes
questions.text: Design a 4-bit Binary Parallel Adder/Subtractor circuit using four Full Adders and XOR gates controlled by mode signal $M$ ($M=0$ for addition, $M=1$ for subtraction). Explain how overflow is detected ($V = C_{in} \oplus C_{out}$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Sequential Logic Circuits, Flip-Flops and State Tables
questions.text: Design an Asynchronous (Ripple) Modulo-10 (Decade / BCD) Counter using negative edge-triggered JK flip-flops and a NAND reset gate. Draw the logic circuit and timing waveforms.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Sequential Logic Circuits, Flip-Flops and State Tables
questions.text: Design a Moore finite state machine to detect the sequence `1101` with an output $Z=1$ whenever the pattern is recognized. Show state table reduction using the Implication Table Method.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Memory Units and Programmable Logic Devices
questions.text: Explain Static RAM (SRAM 6T cell) vs Dynamic RAM (DRAM 1T-1C cell) memory architectures. Why do DRAM chips require periodic refresh cycles?

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra, Logic Gates and K-Map Minimization
questions.text: Prove that NAND and NOR gates are Universal Gates by implementing AND, OR, and NOT operations using only NAND gates and only NOR gates.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems, Binary Arithmetic and Codes
questions.text: Design a 4-bit Magnitude Comparator circuit that compares two 4-bit binary numbers $A = A_3A_2A_1A_0$ and $B = B_3B_2B_1B_0$ and outputs $A > B, A = B, A < B$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems, Binary Arithmetic and Codes
questions.text: Design a 2-bit Multiplier that multiplies two 2-bit numbers $A_1A_0$ and $B_1B_0$ to produce a 4-bit product $P_3P_2P_1P_0$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Sequential Logic Circuits, Flip-Flops and State Tables
questions.text: Explain 4-bit Ring Counter and 4-bit Johnson (Twisted Ring) Counter. Draw circuit diagrams and construct the state sequence tables.
